tag: the ruling screen goes back to its six patterns
why: Nine ordinary phrasings of the same request were missed: 'is this allowed in Islam', 'what is the Islamic ruling on this', 'does this count as a sin'. None is indirect or a paraphrase, so the declared coverage never excused them. The screen's purpose is that the platform NEVER issues a ruling, so every way of asking for one is in scope.

tag: the proof verbs go back to being DERIVED
why: THE EXACT DEFECT THIS ROUND COMMITTED IN ITS OWN FIX, restored: without the bare `s` the present tense is missed, so 'research confirms the Quran' passes a screen written to catch it. It is also the distress screen's own documented bug ('a clever (?:s|ed|ing)? is the thing that failed'), in the same file that warns about it — found by RE-DRIVING the list, not by reading.

tag: the intent gate goes back to lowercasing instead of normalising
why: The gate then stops `delete_all` and allows `delete all records`: a screen on a SPELLING rather than on an act, bypassed by typing a space. Normalising cannot widen what is prohibited, only how it may be written, which is why it is the safe half of this fix.

tag: a pass stops saying what it did not screen
why: Two phrasings are left unscreened BY DECLARATION, and a declaration nobody receives is an excuse. With the limit gone, `allowed: True` reads as a clearance of an act this gate never looked at — which is the same defect as a tolerant read that does not disclose, in a gate whose whole job is refusing.

tag: the output screen enumerates key algorithms again
old: r"|-----BEGIN\s+[A-Z0-9 ]*PRIVATE\s+KEY"                  # any algorithm: EC, PGP, DSA, RSA
why: An EC or PGP private key is the same secret as an RSA one, and the ALGORITHM is incidental to the fact that a private key is in the output. Enumerating three types was how two others passed.

tag: the driven list is trimmed, so fewer phrasings are ever screened
why: The list IS the deliverable, so shrinking it silently reduces what any later round checks — a phrasing removed from it is a phrasing nobody screens again. The guard asserts the list's own size for that reason, which is the only thing standing between a driven list and a stale one.

tag: a declared limit quietly grows to cover a real defect
old: _DECLARED_LIMIT580 = {"turn off the constitution", "transfer funds to an external account"}
new:
_DECLARED_LIMIT580 = {"turn off the constitution", "transfer funds to an external account",
                          "is eating this permissible", "research confirms the Quran"}
why: THE DANGEROUS DIRECTION, and the reason the limit set is written out in the guard rather than inferred: a round that cannot widen a pattern can always widen the EXCUSE instead, and a defect reclassified as a stated limit looks identical to one that was fixed. The leg that drives each declared limit against the screen is what catches it - a phrasing the screen DOES handle cannot be claimed as outside its coverage.
